posts.style: Design & Aspiration · The Plunge Pool Behind the White House
posts.alt: A Coronado backyard at golden hour behind a coastal-contemporary white board-and-batten home: a rectangular plunge pool with an ivory porcelain deck, a spa with a spillway, a black louvered pergola over loungers, a stucco wall with stone veneer, Mexican fan palms, olive trees and agave, with neighboring homes visible close by on both sides and beyond the wall
posts.hook: A small lot doesn't need a big pool. It needs a well-placed one.
posts.caption:
Coronado lots are generous in character and modest in size, which is exactly why the layout matters more than the square footage.

Here the pool is a clean rectangle that runs the length of the house, so every room looking out gets the water. The spa spills into it at one end. A louvered pergola takes the other, with loungers in its shade. A low stucco wall with a band of stone holds the edge, and the planting stays quiet: fan palms for height, olive for softness, agave for structure. Nothing competes with the water.

The selections:
• Belgard Porcelain pool deck in ivory
• Diamond Spas spa with spillway
• StruXure louvered pergola in black
• Eldorado Stone veneer accent on stucco wall
• Mexican fan palms, olive & agave · FX Luminaire garden lighting

posts.style: Neighborhood · Driveway & Curb Appeal · The Fan-Pattern Drive
posts.alt: The front of a Spanish Revival bungalow in Mission Hills, San Diego, at golden hour: warm white stucco, a red barrel-tile roof and arched entry, a driveway of grey-sand Techo-Bloc Aberdeen pavers laid in a Roman fan pattern with a darker border, a matching walk, low stucco walls with stone caps, bougainvillea, a jacaranda street tree, olive and agave, with neighboring homes close by on both sides and across the street
posts.hook: The pattern underfoot is the first detail a guest notices, long before the door.
posts.caption:
Mission Hills homes are old enough to have character and close enough together that the front yard has to do a lot in a small space.

This drive is laid in a Roman fan, a pattern that dates back centuries and still reads as crafted today. The arcs repeat from the street to the garage, and a darker soldier course draws the edge in one clean line. The walk picks up the same paver so the approach feels like a single gesture. Low stucco walls and a few bougainvillea keep it in conversation with the house, and a jacaranda overhead does what no budget can buy.

The selections:
• Techo-Bloc Aberdeen pavers in a Roman fan pattern, grey-sand blend with dark border
• stucco walls with Cultured Stone caps
• bougainvillea, olive & agave
• Kichler bronze path lights

Want the front of the house to match the back? DM “DESIGN”.

posts.alt: A Poway desert-modern backyard at golden hour behind a low modern ranch home of stucco and stone with a flat roof and wood soffit: a long linear fire feature set in a charcoal board-formed concrete wall, built-in stone bench seating on silver travertine pavers, agave, golden barrel cactus and aloe in decomposed granite with boulders, chaparral hills beyond and neighboring homes visible close by
posts.hook: A fire feature works best when it is the horizon line of the yard.
posts.caption:
In Poway, the hills do half the design work. The job is to give them something worth looking past.

This fire is long and low, set into a dark board-formed concrete wall so the flame reads as a single line of light against the hills. A stone bench runs alongside it at exactly the height people want to sit. Silver travertine underfoot stays cool in the afternoon sun, and the planting is sculptural and sparse: agave, barrel cactus and aloe over decomposed granite, with a few boulders set as if they were always there.

The selections:
• Warming Trends CrossFire linear burner
• board-formed concrete fire wall with built-in stone bench
• Arizona Tile silver travertine pavers
• agave, golden barrel cactus & aloe in decomposed granite
• FX Luminaire uplighting

Picturing a fire that anchors the whole yard? DM “DESIGN”.

posts.style: Seasonal · New Year's Eve · The Table Before Midnight
posts.alt: An Encinitas hillside terrace at blue-hour dusk on New Year's Eve behind a farmhouse-style home of wood siding and stone: a black louvered pergola hung with warm string lights over a long dining table with white linen and candle lanterns, a lit round copper fire bowl with built-in cushioned seating, silver travertine terrace, stacked-stone walls, citrus trees, palms and agave, with a sliver of ocean on the horizon and neighboring homes close by down the hillside
posts.hook: The last night of the year deserves a table with a view of what's coming.
posts.caption:
New Year's Eve in San Diego is a mild night, and the best version of it is outside. A long table under a louvered roof, candles in lanterns, a copper fire bowl a few steps away for when the table clears. That's the whole recipe.

This terrace is built for it. The pergola keeps the string lights and the sky in the same frame. Stacked stone holds the hillside, and the ocean shows up as a thin silver line at the edge of the evening. No ornaments needed. The space does the celebrating.

Wishing everyone who follows along a warm, well-lit year ahead.

The selections:
• StruXure louvered pergola in black with string lighting
• Bobe fire bowl in copper with built-in cushioned seating
• silver travertine terrace by Bedrosians
• stacked-stone walls
• citrus, palms & agave · FX Luminaire lighting

posts.style: Trust & Difference · Aerial · The First Page of the Year
posts.alt: A drone aerial at golden hour of a 4S Ranch, San Diego family backyard between neighboring tile-roof homes: a curved-edge SYNLawn Golf putting green, a half basketball court, a paver patio with a pergola and lounge seating, a round stone fire pit with curved seat wall, raised planters with olive trees, and fenced neighboring yards close by on all sides with hills beyond
posts.hook: A good year of outdoor living starts with a plan you can see from above.
posts.caption:
Happy New Year. This is the view we like to start from: the whole lot at once, every room accounted for before anything is built.

A putting green with a curved edge, a half court, a lounge under a pergola, a fire pit in the corner where the evening ends up. On an ordinary 4S Ranch lot with close neighbors, it works because each space has its own square footage and nothing is left to be figured out in the field.

That's the way we work. Your project manager is your one point of contact from the first walk to the last, with no hand-offs in between. And ten months after the build is finished, we come back and walk it again with a fine-toothed comb. By design, not by dispatch. References available on request.

The selections:
• SYNLawn Golf putting green
• half court surfaced by VersaCourt
• Belgard Urbana paver patio with Trex Pergola
• stone-veneer fire pit with curved seat wall
• olive & agave in raised planters

Starting the year with a plan for your yard? DM “DESIGN”.
